near_miss.why_not: Father+mother co-ordination is universal; ON pivots are Christian godparent law (guðsifjar), Vedic/epic contexts unrelated (cosmic triads, Cirakārin's dilemma); no shared figure beyond the kin pair.

near_miss.lead: lists of female kin (mother, sister, daughter)
near_miss.why_not: ON lists are canon-law incest degrees (Leviticus-derived); AVP mātṛhā pitṛhā svasṛhā is a list of kin-slayers, ORV a narrative of women brought; enumeration of kin terms is not a formula.

near_miss.lead: triad mother-sister-daughter as women barred sexually (ON incest law ~ MBh 'treat others' wives like mother, sister, daughter')
near_miss.why_not: Closest of the kin bundles: same three cognate kin terms in a sexual-ethics context. But the triad is the natural first circle of forbidden women, ON text is Christian canon law, MBh is a simile about others' wives (different syntax); chance/universal.

near_miss.lead: identification as 'daughter of X, sister of Y'
near_miss.why_not: ON is saga genealogy, AV a charm addressing a plant as daughter of Asuras, sister of gods; genealogical identification by kin terms is generic.
No shared collocation; law procedure vs concord charm.
ǫl ~ alus is a Balto-Germanic lexical isogloss, not a phrase: ON 'samburðar ǫl' (club-ale at Yule) vs Latvian 'dzeriet ... alutiņu' (drink beer); different collocates, late Latvian dainas.

near_miss.lead: sleep/dream/waking scenes (sofa, dreyma ~ ἔγρετο ἐξ ὕπνου; suptā)
near_miss.why_not: No cognate collocation; ON 'illa sef ek / mart dreymir mik' vs Homeric divine dream; generic narrative.
Partner irrelevant; 'word/rumour flies' figure (fama volat, φήμη) not carried by cognates (fljúga vs πέτομαι/volo).
Partner is Cato's recipe; weapon-biting is Germanic-internal (OE bītan of swords), no cross-branch cognate witness found.

near_miss.lead: birth-and-naming: 'ól ... barn ok var sá sveinn nefndr Hákon' ~ MIr 'co mbert mac dó, Aengus a ainm' / 'beirid sí mac ocus bertha ainm do'
near_miss.why_not: Narrative 'bore a son, named N' is universal; ON verb is ala, not bera, and nefna vs ainm do-beir differ in construction; Irish naming clause is Irish idiom.

near_miss.lead: lying at night with the troop (lágu um nætr ~ въ ту нощь лежащю)
near_miss.why_not: Lie + night is everyday chronicle narrative; no figure.

near_miss.lead: bera + fire (ber ... elda ~ bhárāma idhmám, agnaú ... bhare)
near_miss.why_not: Skaldic 'snarpra elda sárflóðs' is a sword-kenning (fires of wound-flood) object of nothing like 'bring fuel'; 'snilld ber' = eloquence surpasses; no congruence with Vedic offering to Agni.

near_miss.lead: woman singing at the quern ('kvað við forkunnar fagrt er hon mól') with a king listening
near_miss.why_not: Irish partners irrelevant. Searched: Plutarch Sept. sap. conv. 14 'ᾀδούσης πρὸς τὴν μύλην ... ἄλει μύλα ἄλει · καὶ γὰρ Πιττακὸς ἄλει ... βασιλεύων' and Od. 20.106 μύλαι — a shared theme (mill-song, king, erotic undertone) but no cognate wording (ἀλέω/ᾄδω vs mala/kveða; only μύλη ~ mala root) and grinding songs are a universal work-song genre.
ON is cutting out a tongue (miracle story), MBh weapon-as-tongue metaphor; no shared figure.

error.correct_reading: ro theich, pret. 3sg of teichid 'flees' (< *tekʷ-), not téit 'goes'
error.evidence: 'a ingin ro theigh ro folaig ría German' = his daughter fled and hid from Germanus

error.correct_reading: thes = (a)tess 'in the south' (adverb, cf. dess 'right, south'), not téit
error.evidence: 'Atā ag Rosaigh na Rīgh thes' = he is at Rosach na Ríg in the south

note: Second reading of 18 flagged bundles; mostly ON Christian law kin lists and Heimskringla narrative against Vedic/epic/Greek partners; no claim defensible; 13 near-misses, 2 errors.
